Definition: A folder that holds everything for one program: its code, its scenes and its resources, like pictures and models.
A ready-made starting project. Quorum Studio copies it when you make a new project.
A file ending in .qs that stores a scene: its layers, items, lights and cameras.
JavaScript Object Notation, a plain text format for data. Scene files, tilesets, terrain files and material files are all JSON.
A set of pictures or 3D models, with a JSON file that names and describes each one, so they can appear in the palette.
One part of a scene with its own camera, such as a 3D world with a 2D display drawn on top of it.
The ground of a 3D world: hills, valleys and flat land. Quorum stores it as heights, in a folder of its own.
A picture wrapped onto the surface of a 3D object, such as a photo of grass or bricks.
A description of how a surface looks: its texture pictures, and settings such as how shiny or bumpy it is.
The picture of a surface's colors, like a photo of it taken in flat, even light.
A picture that stores which way each tiny bit of a surface faces, so bumps and cracks catch the light even on a flat surface.
A picture that says which parts of a surface are rough and dull and which are smooth and shiny.
A picture that darkens the gaps and corners of a surface that light has trouble reaching.
A picture that says which parts of a surface stick up and which sink down. On terrain, it helps materials blend where they meet.
A picture for one region of a terrain that records how much of each material shows at each point, so you can paint grass in one place and rock in another.
